newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rebels kill 11 soldiers in ambush.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rebels kill 11 soldiers in ambush.

text.p: Separatist Tamil Tiger guerrillas on Friday attacked a Sri Lankan army patrol in the country's northeast, killing 11 soldiers and wounding seven, army officials said.

The party of 27 troops was ambushed near the remote town of Kebitigollewa in Anuradhapura district as they set out in the morning to clear the area's roads of land mines and explosives planted there by the guerrillas at night.
The attack was the latest in a series of recent strikes on government and military targets in the region.
On Tuesday, a Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) suicide bomber killed one of eastern Sri Lanka's senior police commando officers.
The bomber rammed his motorcycle into the car of the deputy chief of the police Special Task Force (STF) in Batticaloa district, near Karativu, about 240 km (150 miles) east of Colombo.
In a separate incident the same day, seven soldiers were killed in the northeastern village of Weli Oya when soldiers bathing in an irrigation tank set off a mine laid underwater by the rebels.
On Thursday, rebels attacked another mine-clearing party in the eastern town of Kiran, killing one soldier and wounding another, the Defence Ministry said.

The Tigers, who are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in the island's north and east, overran an STF camp at Pulukunava in eastern Amparai district last week, killing 36 security personnel. It was the Tigers' biggest attack on government forces in more than two months.
The military launched an offensive against guerrilla jungle bases shortly after the attack, destroying several abandoned rebel camps, but there was no immediate word on guerrilla casualties.
The government says more than 50,000 people have died in the war, now in its 14th year. The Tigers say the death toll is much higher.
